rationale: The workflow already satisfies the dependency-caching intent of P-LIT-GHA-CACHE through ruby/setup-ruby@v1 with bundler-cache: true, which caches Bundler dependencies into vendor/bundle (matching BUNDLE_PATH). P-LIT-GHA-CACHE lists "An equivalent cache already exists" as a contraindication, so adding a separate actions/cache for the same dependency state would be redundant and is not supported. No other pattern fits: there is no matrix for fail-fast (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST), no schedule to cancel or suppress (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE, P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE), no completion history for history-based timeouts (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT; ci_history shows no completed runs), a single job so job gating/reordering does not apply (P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST, P-LIT-PRIORITIZE, P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY), no tests to select or prioritize (P-LIT-SELECT, P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT), no Bazel build (P-LIT-BAZEL-*), and the three Jekyll builds are intentional for profiling/memory analysis and must be preserved. The workflow is workflow_dispatch-only with one job, so skip/change-filter optimizations would alter required-check semantics without a policy basis. Preserving intended build/test coverage and avoiding unrelated changes, no supported optimization applies.
